missing_supported_requirements.why_missing: Section provides many climate metrics/targets but does not clearly link metrics to each sustainability-related risk/opportunity that could reasonably be expected to affect prospects, nor explicitly identify which metrics are required by applicable IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards for each such risk/opportunity.

Metrics are listed (GHG, financed emissions, high-carbon exposure, internal carbon price) but not mapped to specific sustainability-related risks/opportunities and how each metric monitors those risks/opportunities.

Some metrics/targets are not labelled/defined with sufficient clarity/precision (eg 'All-scopes target' baseline value lacks unit; internal carbon price table repeats 'Investment decisions' with different prices without clear differentiation; listed equity table lacks identifiers/definitions for the multiple rows).
No disclosure of revisions to targets (or an explicit statement that there were no revisions) and explanations for revisions, despite the requirement to disclose revisions if any.
Section mentions a correction to Scope 1 but does not address consistency over time for metrics/targets or explain whether any metric was redefined/replaced and how comparability is maintained.

Comparatives are provided for financed emissions (2022–2024) but not for most other amounts disclosed (eg Scope 1/2/Scope 3 business travel, high-carbon exposure, internal carbon prices, carbon credits).
A correction is mentioned for Scope 1, but there is no revised comparative amount disclosed for the preceding period(s) where the error/estimate affected comparatives (if applicable).
No disclosure of the difference between previously disclosed comparative amounts and revised comparative amounts related to the Scope 1 correction (if applicable).

While a correction is referenced, the section does not explain the reasons for revising comparative amounts (and does not present revised comparatives), as required when new information affects prior estimates.
If the Scope 1 'correction' constitutes a redefinition/replacement, the section does not provide revised comparative amounts (or state impracticability).

The section does not clearly explain changes to the metric definition/approach (beyond a brief note about a correction) in a way that satisfies the 'explain the changes' requirement when metrics are redefined/replaced.
No explanation of reasons for changes (and why the change provides more useful information) related to the Scope 1 correction/redefinition, if applicable.
Scope 3 business travel is presented for 2024 only; if this is a new metric, the section does not provide a comparative amount or state impracticability.

Where comparatives are not provided (eg Scope 1/2/Scope 3 travel, high-carbon exposure, internal carbon price, carbon credits), the section does not state that revising/providing comparatives is impracticable (if that is the reason).
Section does not state that operational GHG emissions are measured in accordance with the GHG Protocol Corporate Standard (or disclose an alternative required method).

Operational GHG measurement approach inputs/assumptions are only partially described (eg Scope 2 market-based narrative); lacks a coherent description of measurement approach, key inputs and assumptions for Scope 1/2/Scope 3.
No disclosure of why the chosen measurement approaches/inputs/assumptions were selected for GHG emissions.
Mentions a Scope 1 correction but does not clearly describe changes to measurement approach/inputs/assumptions during the period and reasons (beyond the brief correction note).
No disaggregation of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions between the consolidated accounting group and other investees (associates/JVs/unconsolidated subsidiaries) as required.
No disclosure of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions for other investees excluded from the consolidated accounting group disaggregation.
No explicit disclosure of Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions attributable to associates/joint ventures/unconsolidated subsidiaries (if any), or confirmation that none exist.

Location-based Scope 2 is disclosed and some contractual instrument narrative is provided for market-based, but the disclosure does not clearly provide the information about contractual instruments necessary to understand Scope 2 (eg volumes/coverage, instrument types, quality/eligibility, boundaries) in a complete way.

Scope 3 categories included are not comprehensively listed; only business travel and financed emissions (Category 15) are shown, without stating whether other Scope 3 categories are excluded/not measured.

required_fixes: Add an explicit mapping of disclosed metrics/targets to the climate-related (and other sustainability-related, if applicable) risks and opportunities that could reasonably be expected to affect prospects, indicating which metrics are required by IFRS S2 (and any other applicable IFRS SDS) versus entity-defined metrics (IFRS S1.46).

Improve labelling/definitions: specify units for all baselines/targets (eg 'All-scopes target' baseline), clarify duplicated internal carbon price 'Investment decisions' rows, and explain what each listed equity row represents (IFRS S1.53).
Provide comparative information for preceding period(s) for all disclosed amounts, or explicitly state impracticability where applicable (IFRS S1.B49, B53, B54).

Address the Scope 1 'correction' under the comparative revision requirements: disclose revised comparative amounts (if prior-period figures were affected), quantify differences, and explain reasons; or clarify that no prior-period amounts were affected (IFRS S1.B50/B52).

State GHG measurement standard used (GHG Protocol Corporate Standard 2004 or jurisdictional alternative) and provide a coherent description of measurement approach, key inputs/assumptions, reasons for choices, and changes during the period (IFRS S2.29(a)(ii)–(iii)).

Provide required Scope 1/2 disaggregation between consolidated accounting group and other investees (associates/JVs/unconsolidated subsidiaries/other investees), or explicitly state that there are none (IFRS S2.29(a)(iv)).
For Scope 3, list the categories included in the Scope 3 measure and clarify which categories are excluded/not measured (IFRS S2.29(a)(vi)(1)).
If any targets were revised, disclose revisions and explanations; if none, consider stating 'no revisions during 2024' to avoid ambiguity (IFRS S1.51(g)).
ifrs_coverage_judge.summary: The section provides substantial quantitative climate metrics and targets (Scopes 1–3, financed emissions, high-carbon exposure, internal carbon pricing, targets and progress). However, it does not meet several supported IFRS S1/S2 requirements: it lacks clear linkage of metrics to specific risks/opportunities, lacks broad comparative information, does not properly address the Scope 1 correction under comparative revision guidance, omits required GHG measurement standard/approach rationale disclosures, and omits Scope 1/2 disaggregation between consolidated group and other investees. No invented missing-data statements were found.

evidence_judge.summary: Several quantitative disclosures are well-supported (e.g., financed emissions from loans, internal carbon prices, many target parameters), but there are clear evidence-mapping gaps for the reporting boundary basis and for two operational emissions metrics (Scope 2 location-based and Scope 3 business travel). Additional issues include incomplete evidence mapping for listed equity market values and potentially inconsistent/unevidenced total assets used as the denominator for high-carbon exposure. Qualitative assertions like 'on track' and third-party 'validation' need clearer substantiation or definitions.

voice_issues: Voice is consistently neutral and descriptive; however, it does not explicitly adopt a single POV convention (first-person plural vs third-person). This is a minor issue because the section largely avoids pronouns altogether.
structure_issues: Layered structure is mostly followed (overview → tables → brief commentary), but several subsections end abruptly without a short connectivity sentence linking to related sections or financial statements.

The section does not explicitly separate general sustainability metrics (IFRS S1) from climate-specific metrics (IFRS S2); everything is presented under climate-related framing, which is acceptable here but slightly short of the requested explicit separation.

Some complex metrics (e.g., high‑carbon sector exposure, internal carbon pricing) could benefit from a short methodology/limitations paragraph following the tables or bullets to fully align with the ‘boundary → inputs → calculation → limitations → governance’ pattern.
wording_issues: A few sentences are relatively long and could be split for maximum clarity (e.g., the Scope 2 market-based note and the PCAF proxy description).

The phrase “on track” for target status is acceptable but could be made more standards-oriented by briefly indicating the basis for that assessment (e.g., comparison to interim milestones) to reinforce evidence-led language.

The section generally uses standards-oriented verbs, but some opportunities remain to emphasize definitional phrasing (e.g., explicitly stating “Metric is defined as…” for high‑carbon sector exposure and internal carbon prices).
table_figure_issues: All tables are numbered and captioned clearly and are introduced in nearby narrative, which aligns well with the style guide.

Table 3 (Listed equity holdings) presents multiple rows with identical labels and years; while this may reflect underlying data, a total row or brief explanatory note (e.g., that rows represent different portfolios or mandates) would improve traceability.

Table 4 (Internal carbon prices) includes two rows labelled “Investment decisions” with different prices and applications; this may be accurate but could confuse readers without a clarifying note (e.g., different use cases or time horizons).

Table 5 (Emissions data quality and estimation mix) is clear but would benefit from a short narrative note on how these categories are defined and any limitations, to fully meet the transparency and evidence rules.
required_fixes: Add brief connectivity sentences at the end of key subsections (e.g., 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7) that reference related narrative or financial statement areas using generic placeholders such as “Refer to [Section: Strategy – Climate-related risks and opportunities]” or “See [Appendix: Methodologies]”.

Clarify the duplicated labels in Table 4 by either (a) differentiating the two “Investment decisions” rows (e.g., by adding qualifiers in the Application label) or (b) adding a short note below the table explaining why multiple internal prices apply to the same application category.

For high‑carbon sector exposure (Section 4.4) and internal carbon pricing (Section 4.5), add one short paragraph each that defines the metric boundary and key methodological choices (e.g., sector classification basis, asset classes included, whether exposures are gross or net, and any key exclusions).

For Table 3, add either a total row or a short explanatory note indicating what each listed equity row represents (e.g., different portfolios, strategies, or sub‑segments) to improve traceability and audit readiness.

In Section 4.7, add a short narrative paragraph defining each data quality category at a high level and briefly describing limitations and how they may affect comparability, in line with the evidence and missing‑data rules.

Optionally, make the POV convention explicit at the start of the Metrics and Targets chapter (e.g., “We disclose…” or “The bank discloses…”) and apply consistently in future sections, even though this section already avoids inconsistent pronoun use.
style_judge.summary: The section is well-structured, neutral, and largely aligned with the IFRS-style, audit-ready disclosure voice. Tables are clearly captioned and introduced, metrics and targets are defined with appropriate detail, and there is no promotional or reference-company content. Minor improvements are needed around connectivity sentences, clarifying duplicated labels in the internal carbon pricing table, adding brief methodological notes for certain metrics, and enhancing the explanation of data quality categories. With these targeted edits, the section would be fully aligned with the approved authoring style.
